guard: A take still waiting when its connection closes ends with that connection, the probe it falls back to included, so a read waiting on it returns and the request can be taken again on the new link
why: nats.js settles a no-mux request only from its reply subscription, and a connection that closes
first closes that subscription without settling it. A take in flight across a reconnect then never
ends, and the holder reuses it for every later read, so the request is never shown.
The suite imports @cotal-ai/core through its package export, so the command builds core before each
run and the mutation rebuilds it after restore.

mutations.name: a take waits on its own reply subscription only
mutations.find: return await Promise.race([this.askTake(nc, role, seq, id, count, epoch), closed]);
mutations.replace: return await this.askTake(nc, role, seq, id, count, epoch);
mutations.expectRed: 11a a read waiting on that take ends with the old link, well before its wait runs out, and shows nothing
mutations.cell: 11a a read waiting on that take ends with the old link, well before its wait runs out, and shows nothing
mutations.note: The take never settles once its connection closes, so the read waits out its whole wait and every later read reuses the stuck take.

mutations.name: a take that falls back to the probe waits on the probe's reply only
mutations.find: return await Promise.race([this.askTake(nc, role, seq, id, count, epoch), closed]);
mutations.replace: return await this.askTake(nc, role, seq, id, count, epoch);
mutations.expectRed: 11e with nothing serving the take rail, a read waiting on the probe the take falls back to ends with the old link too
mutations.cell: 11e with nothing serving the take rail, a read waiting on the probe the take falls back to ends with the old link too
mutations.note: With nothing on the take rail the take asks the anycastTakes probe on ctl.delivery, another no-mux request. Unraced, it never settles once its connection closes, and every later read reuses the stuck take.
